# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Deaf monkey. I can see the bomb but can't hear anything. I need to communicate what I see to the others via speech (heard by Mute and Blind) and gestures (seen only by Mute).

Since this is the first turn, I should share my observations. I can use speech (which both Mute and Blind will hear) to describe the bomb's display, light, and wires.

Let me report what I see clearly, since this is the initial round and nobody has any info yet.

```
speak(text="Display shows 8. Light is green. Wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

I received a gesture from Mute (☝ - pointing up, could mean "first" or "one" or drawing attention to something). Since I already spoke my info last turn, and gestures don't carry to Blind, Mute is trying to signal something to me specifically - likely acknowledging or asking about wire 1, or indicating something about the manual regarding a specific wire/step.

Since Mute cannot speak and can only gesture to me, and I can't hear Mute's silence, I should wait to see if more gestures clarify, but I could also try responding to confirm receipt or ask for clarification via gesture. However, gestures are simple symbols - I could try gesturing back "☝" to confirm I understand they mean wire 1, or gesture "❓"-like acknowledgment (not available). Let me just acknowledge with a matching gesture to confirm receipt, and wait for more info before speaking further since I don't want to give wrong instructions to Blind without confirming what Mute needs.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new information arrived this turn. Mute may be waiting for Blind to speak, or processing my gesture confirmation. Since the board hasn't changed, I don't have new visual info to share. I'll wait to see what develops - Blind speaks after Mute in the turn order, so I should wait to hear from them (though I can't hear speech) - actually I never receive speech at all. I only receive gestures from Mute.

Since nothing new happened, I'll wait and see if Mute sends more gestures based on what Blind said (which I can't hear).

```
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Still nothing new. The board is unchanged. I already shared the full bomb state (display 8, green light, wires red/yellow/blue) in turn 1, and confirmed Mute's gesture with my own gesture in turn 2. Since I speak and both Mute and Blind hear me, my initial info should have reached them both. 

Perhaps they are waiting on each other to coordinate the actual action (Blind needs to act based on Mute's manual knowledge combined with my visual info, which reached Blind too since I spoke it).

I'll wait again since I have nothing new to report and don't want to spam repeated info that could cause confusion.

```
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Nothing has changed for several turns. Let me reconsider - perhaps my initial speech didn't clearly land or they need reconfirmation. Since repeating costs little and could help synchronize, let me restate the bomb's current state clearly again in case it was missed or in case Blind needs reminding since they can't see the board themselves and rely entirely on what I say.

```
speak(text="Reminder: Display shows 8. Light is green. Wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue. No changes since last report.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

Mute gestured ☝ to me again - the same gesture as before. This is a repeated signal. Since gestures only carry symbols with no inherent meaning until we establish one, and Mute cannot speak, they may be trying to ask me something specific or confirm something about "one" - possibly wire 1, or confirming the first digit/step.

Since I can't establish complex meaning through single gestures alone, and Mute is repeating the same gesture, perhaps this is an acknowledgment protocol - like "received" or "yes, wire 1 is relevant." 

Let me try acknowledging again, and also try to open a more useful channel - since I can gesture back symbols, maybe I should try building a simple protocol. Let me gesture back to confirm "wire 1" understanding using ☝ then try pointing to red conceptually isn't possible without established meaning.

Actually, the most productive thing is to keep acknowledging consistently so Mute knows I'm receiving, and continue waiting for Blind's action since I already gave full info via speech.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

Mute keeps sending ☝ repeatedly - this seems to be a consistent, deliberate signal, not just random. Since Mute cannot speak and I cannot hear, this gesture must be their only way to communicate with me. They might be trying to ask "is it wire 1?" or confirm "wire 1" repeatedly because they need me to confirm something specific about wire 1, or they're stuck waiting for my confirmation before proceeding.

Since I already told them (via speech, which they can hear) that wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue - maybe they're using ☝ to ask "confirm wire 1 is the one to cut" or similar, expecting me to gesture back a confirmation.

Let me try a different response this time - instead of just mirroring ☝, let me try to give more specific gesture feedback. Since Blind cannot see gestures, gestures are purely for Mute. Let me try using two gestures to indicate "wire 1 red" - perhaps ✊(for stop/red-ish) is too presumptuous without shared vocabulary.

Given the constraint, the safest approach: keep confirming with ☝ to show consistent acknowledgment, since Mute seems to want that confirmation loop closed.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

This loop isn't progressing - Mute keeps sending the same single gesture ☝ and I keep mirroring it, but nothing is advancing. I need to break this pattern and think more carefully.

Let me reconsider the setup: Mute reads the manual, sees no bomb. I see the bomb, hear nothing. Blind touches the bomb, sees/hears nothing. 

Mute needs my visual info to know what the manual's instructions apply to (since the manual likely says something like "if wire X is red, do Y"). I already spoke that info - Mute should have heard it since Mute hears speech. So Mute has my data already.

The repeated ☝ from Mute might mean "wire 1" as their way of confirming back to me which wire matters per the manual - like "the manual says wire 1 matters" - but this doesn't require action from me since I can't touch anything.

Actually - Mute needs to talk to Blind, not me! Mute speaks to convey manual instructions to Blind (who can hear). I'm receiving gestures meant to confirm something with me, but the real action needs Mute speaking to Blind directly, telling them what to do with the wires based on the manual + my visual report.

My job now: just confirm I understand, and let Mute proceed to instruct Blind via speech. I should stop repeating and perhaps signal something new to show I'm listening for their next move, or just wait to let the real coordination (Mute→Blind via speech) happen.

```
wait()
```
